function.name: give_up
function.arguments: {"reason": "Three in-place closes all read back 0.016-0.022 (jaws fully closed on air) and the lift test at step 474 showed the block stayed on the table, so the block was never captured. With 2 of 20 policy calls left I cannot do close plus transport plus release, so the task is not completable in the remaining budget. The block is still loose on the table at about x=-0.02, y=-0.006; the blue bowl is at about x=+0.15.", "hindsight": "Concrete facts for this rig (robosuite Panda plus bowl task, inspect-robots move_to adapter). (1) The tool layer runs only a few control steps when a command changes arm dimensions alone (2-10 steps, about 9 mm per step), so the arm reaches only 20-40 percent of the commanded distance; that burned about 10 of my 20 calls on a slow descent. A gripper latch change costs about 80 steps, so always pair arm targets with a gripper command (for example gripper=1 plus z=0.80) to make the arm actually arrive: that trick got me from z=0.876 to z=0.824 in one call. (2) eef_pos sits well above the fingertips: at z=0.876 the pads were still above the 2 cm block and closing gave air; the pads only straddled the block at z about 0.82-0.84, and the arm seems blocked near z=0.82 (fingertips on the table). Plan the final approach to z about 0.83, not 0.87. (3) The measured gripper value is a reliable grasp check: 0.016-0.022 means closed on air, a 2 cm block should read about 0.25-0.3. Read it back before attempting any transport. (4) Camera mapping: front-view horizontal is world y (front camera looks along -x, image-right is +y); side-view horizontal is world x with the robot base on the -x side and the bowl farther in +x. The wrist camera is rolled so its horizontal is roughly the jaw-separation axis, so it must not be read as world x/y. Use the front view to centre the block along the jaw axis and the side view for x. (5) Jaw span is 8 cm and the block 2 cm, so the block centre must be within about 2.5 cm of the TCP along the jaw axis; my residual offset kept the block overlapping one pad, and the closing pad swept it aside instead of trapping it. (6) The block was nudged a few mm in +x during low lateral sweeps, so finish x/y alignment before the last descent, not after. (7) Table surface z=0.80; in this scene the block was near x=-0.02, y=-0.006 and the bowl near x=+0.15, y=-0.015."}
